logline: A villager kid lives behind a 40-block wall that old Tomas raises every morning, and climbs it to see what's out there.
question: why tf is the village wall forty blocks high with no gate?
premise: A plains village sits inside a stone-brick wall 40 blocks high with no gate. Every dawn a little dirt pokes over the rim from outside, and old Tomas, the mason, climbs up and builds one block higher above it. A block of the wall once vanished; Tomas patched it by noon. Tomas is the only one who has been outside: he came in an old minecart before the wall, and he hides when the kids push it. He says there's nothing out there 'we want to trade with'.
twist: The thing outside is a player. The dirt is his pillar (he towers up every morning to look in), the vanished block is the one he mined to peek, the minecart is how players move villagers, and outside the wall is his trading hall: a hundred villagers, each boxed in a one-block cell. The kid reads it as another village where everybody gets their own room. The player at the door looks up at him. The wall was never for monsters; it's for us.

requests.direction: One continuous telling, start to finish: hit only the CAPITALISED words, keep the rest level and quick, no dramatic pauses.
[An old man in his seventies, slow and low, kind but closed]

lines.text: The WALL / around my village / is FORTY blocks high. / Old TOMAS adds / ONE more / every MORNING.
lines.say: The wall around my village is forty blocks HIGH. Old Tomas adds one more every MORNING.
lines.note: one bright breath, proud of the wall like it's the biggest thing in the world

lines.text: A ZOMBIE / can't even jump / TWO blocks. / So what's it FOR?
lines.say: A zombie can't even jump two BLOCKS. So what's it FOR?
lines.note: a kid doing the maths out loud, honestly puzzled on the last words

lines.text: There's no GATE. / I've never SEEN / OUTSIDE.
lines.say: There's no GATE. I've never seen OUTSIDE.
lines.note: matter-of-fact, a little wistful, still bright

lines.text: But every MORNING, / something BROWN / peeks over / the TOP.
lines.say: But every morning, something brown peeks over the TOP.
lines.note: leaning in, telling the strange part; the kid never says what it is (the picture shows dirt)

lines.text: So Tomas CLIMBS up / and builds / one HIGHER.
lines.say: So Tomas climbs up and builds one HIGHER.
lines.note: quick, like it's the most normal chore in the world

lines.direction: slow and low, not turning from the wall

lines.text: Once, a BLOCK / of the wall / just VANISHED. / Tomas had it BACK / by NOON.
lines.say: Once, a block of the wall just VANISHED. Tomas had it back by NOON.
lines.note: amazed at the vanishing, then proud of Tomas

lines.text: Tomas is the ONLY one / who's been OUTSIDE. / He came here / in that old MINECART.
lines.say: Tomas is the only one who's been OUTSIDE. He came here in that old MINECART.
lines.note: a secret everybody knows; lean on the last word

lines.text: When the kids PUSH it, / Tomas RUNS / and HIDES. / I don't know WHY.
lines.say: When the kids push it, Tomas runs and HIDES. I don't know WHY.
lines.note: puzzled, not laughing; the hiding is the strange part

lines.text: I ASKED him / what's OUT there.
lines.say: I asked him what's out THERE.

lines.text: Nothing we want / to TRADE with.
lines.say: Nothing we want to TRADE with.
lines.direction: old and slow, closing the subject, kind but final

lines.text: So before the SUN came up, / I climbed / his LADDER. / All FORTY blocks.
lines.say: So before the sun came up, I climbed his ladder. All forty BLOCKS.
lines.note: sneaky and excited, speeding up as he climbs

lines.text: Outside was / ANOTHER village! / A HUNDRED of us! / EVERYBODY gets / their own ROOM!
lines.say: Outside was another VILLAGE! A hundred of US! Everybody gets their own ROOM!
lines.note: pure delight, the happiest he's been; he thinks it's wonderful

lines.text: Then SOMEONE / by the DOOR / looked UP / at ME.
lines.say: Then someone by the door looked up at ME.
lines.note: the delight stops short; still full voice, a little smaller on the last word
